source_name: PaySpace Magazine (psm7.com) — payments trade press and NBU interviews
why_relevant: Specialist payments/fintech outlet that both reports NBU forward statements ('НБУ планує оновити вимоги до надавачів платіжних послуг') and conducts named interviews with NBU officials (e.g. Oleksii Shaban) that the NBU itself then republishes. Also runs PSM Awards and covers the event circuit, doubling as an event pointer.

source_name: Banker.ua — banking event coverage and regulatory-wave explainers
why_relevant: Covers the Ukrainian banking event circuit (e.g. Ukrainian Banking Summit 2026, Kyiv, 22 May) and publishes consolidated 'regulatory wave' explainers ('Літня хвиля регулювання НБУ: нові вимоги для фінансового ринку') that bundle forthcoming requirements and their effective dates — useful for deadline extraction.

source_name: National FinMon Forum (Ukrainian Compliance Association + LIGA ZAKON) — AML/compliance conference circuit
why_relevant: Compliance-side conference where regulators, lawmakers, systemic-bank compliance officers and international lawyers preview incoming EU-driven financial-monitoring requirements (money mules, new EU AML package). Supervision/AML rules are a large slice of A3 and this circuit is distinct from the payments/fintech one.

source_name: NBU seminars and presentations on financial monitoring (explanatory letters + seminar decks)
why_relevant: Standing NBU page aggregating explanatory letters, seminar materials and presentation decks for supervised institutions. Slide decks from supervisory seminars typically state implementation timelines and expectations more explicitly than the legal acts themselves — a high-yield, low-noise A3 artefact type.

source_name: Mind.ua — UAFIN.TECH and financial-event editorial hub
why_relevant: Business outlet that co-hosts/covers financial conferences and maintains per-event pages summarising themes and speakers; a secondary pointer when organiser sites are stale or paywalled.

source_name: Central Banking — NBU organisation page (speeches and official commentary, international angle)
why_relevant: Central-banking trade press that reports NBU officials' remarks at international conferences and interviews, which is where EU-alignment timelines are often stated for a foreign audience in plainer terms than domestically.

source_name: AFME European Financial Integration Conference — NBU keynote venue
why_relevant: Example of the offshore venue class: NBU First Deputy Governor Serhiy Nikolaychuk gave a keynote at AFME's European Financial Integration Conference 2026 (Frankfurt, 19 May 2026). International industry conferences are where Ukrainian officials state EU-alignment sequencing to a market audience, and these appearances are easily missed by UA-only monitoring.

source_name: old.bank.gov.ua legacy 'Інтерв'ю та виступи' archive
why_relevant: Legacy NBU site category that preserved the dedicated 'Interviews and speeches' listing before the current site merged speeches into the general news feed. Valuable as a historical corpus for lead-time calibration (how long before a rule appeared did an official first mention it), which the current feed makes harder to reconstruct.

source_name: NBU — Consumer Protection hub (Захист прав споживачів)
why_relevant: Central landing page of the NBU consumer-rights function: how to file a complaint (звернення), consumer-protection reports, supervisory expectations and thematic guidance. Root node for the whole cell; changes here typically precede consultations on conduct rules.

source_name: NBU — Quarterly consumer-complaint reports (Захист прав споживачів фінансових послуг: робота зі зверненнями, ZG_YYYY-Qn.pdf)
why_relevant: The core quantitative complaint series for the cell: volumes of written/oral complaints, breakdown by institution type and product (cards, credits, payment operations), and the themes the NBU flags. Trend breaks in a product line are the leading indicator that conduct rules on that product will be tightened.

source_name: NBU — Department for Protection of Financial Services Consumers' Rights (structure page, EN/UA)
why_relevant: Names the actual supervisory unit, its mandate and (usually) its head — the actor map anchor for attributing statements, consultations and enforcement to a specific department. Useful for tracking leadership changes that shift conduct-supervision priorities.

source_name: Unified State Register of Court Decisions (Єдиний державний реєстр судових рішень, ЄДРСР)
why_relevant: Primary full-text corpus of every Ukrainian court decision — civil, commercial, administrative — including consumer-vs-bank disputes, unauthorised debit/card-fraud cases, and banks/PSPs appealing NBU enforcement measures. Free keyword and party search; the single richest raw signal on which rules are actually litigated.

source_name: Opendatabot — ЄДРСР API and court monitoring
why_relevant: Commercial JSON API and alerting layer over the court register — far more tractable than scraping reyestr for continuous monitoring of banks/PSPs as parties, and supports counterparty-level case alerts. The pragmatic collection path for the court-decision half of this cell.

source_name: Supreme Court of Ukraine — press centre / legal positions on consumer-bank disputes
why_relevant: The Supreme Court publicises the doctrinal positions that reshape bank/PSP liability — e.g. that the bank bears the burden of proving customer fault in unauthorised card debits, and that doubts are construed in the consumer's favour. These positions drive both bank product terms and subsequent NBU rulemaking.

source_name: Supreme Court — Judicial practice reviews (Огляди судової практики КЦС/КГС ВС, PDF series)
why_relevant: Periodic curated PDF digests by cassation chamber (civil = consumer/card disputes; commercial = bank/PSP vs regulator and acquiring disputes). Pre-filtered by the court itself, so far cheaper than mining the raw register for doctrinal shifts.

source_name: court.gov.ua — Judiciary portal / case-flow statistics (Стан розгляду справ)
why_relevant: Aggregate caseload and case-status data across Ukrainian courts; supports normalising bank-dispute volumes against total civil/commercial caseload rather than reading raw counts.

source_name: zakon.rada.gov.ua — NBU conduct-supervision regulations (Положення про нагляд за захистом прав споживачів фінансових та обмежених платіжних послуг)
why_relevant: Authoritative consolidated text of the conduct-supervision rulebook (NBU Board Resolution No. 198 of 02.09.2022 and its amendments, incl. Resolution No. 15 of 11.02.2025), covering supervision of banks, non-banks, limited payment service providers and debt-collection conduct. Defines what supervisors can inspect and sanction — the legal frame for every enforcement datapoint in this cell.

source_name: NBU news item — updated conduct-supervision procedure (Актуалізовано порядок нагляду ...)
why_relevant: Concrete example of the regulator announcing a change to the conduct-supervision framework — extending it to limited payment service providers and ethical-behaviour requirements. Exactly the 'next tightening' signal the cell is meant to catch, and shows the announcement pattern to monitor.

source_name: Antimonopoly Committee of Ukraine (АМКУ) — misleading financial-services advertising decisions
why_relevant: A second, routinely-omitted enforcement publisher for consumer harm in banking: АМКУ fines banks under Art. 15-1 of the unfair-competition law for misleading credit advertising (e.g. the UAH 4m+ Ideya Bank '0%' case upheld on appeal). Signals pressure on pricing-disclosure rules independent of the NBU.

source_name: State Service of Ukraine for Food Safety and Consumer Protection (Держпродспоживслужба) — consumer-rights arm
why_relevant: General consumer-protection authority that still publishes explanatory material on financial-services consumer rights and receives consumer complaints; useful for mapping the jurisdictional boundary with the NBU and for catching cross-agency campaigns.

source_name: iplex.com.ua — court decision full texts by register number
why_relevant: Mirror/indexer of ЄДРСР decisions with clean per-decision URLs keyed by register number (doc.php?regnum=...), often more crawlable than the official register and well indexed by search engines — useful as a fallback and for resolving case citations found in press or digests.

source_name: sudovispravy.com.ua — court register search/tracking service
why_relevant: Alternative commercial front-end over the court register with document search and case tracking; a redundancy option if reyestr throttles and Opendatabot licensing is unattractive.

source_name: protocol.ua — practitioner analysis of consumer-vs-bank case law
why_relevant: Lawyer-facing portal that digests Supreme Court positions on card fraud, unauthorised debits and credit disputes with case numbers — a fast pointer into the primary decisions and an early read on where litigation is trending.

source_name: sud.ua — judiciary news and decision reporting
why_relevant: Daily judiciary-news outlet that surfaces newly published Supreme Court positions on payment disputes (e.g. client not liable for bank-merchant settlement after a refund) faster than the court's own digests.

source_name: LIGA:ZAKON / JURLIGA — regulatory commentary on NBU consumer-protection supervision
why_relevant: Consistently covers NBU conduct-supervision rule changes and antitrust risk in financial advertising with links to the underlying resolutions; useful as an early-warning pointer layer around a bot-defended regulator site.

source_name: Academic/legal-scholarship layer on Ukrainian financial-consumer protection (tlaw.nlu.edu.ua, Karazin Journal of Legal Studies)
why_relevant: Peer-reviewed analyses of the legal basis for financial-consumer protection and of the still-unadopted financial ombudsman model — provides the institutional-gap context that explains why complaint volumes concentrate on the NBU and the courts.

source_name: NBU — Payment Services supervision section (Нагляд / Платіжні послуги)
why_relevant: Master hub of the NBU as payments regulator: licensing/authorisation of payment service providers, registration of payment systems and technological operators, registers, and links to the secondary acts implementing the Law on Payment Services. Single best entry point for the whole cell.

source_name: NBU — Registration of payment systems, their participants and technological payment service operators
why_relevant: Procedural rules and register for payment system participants and technological operators — directly binds vendors and acquirers (e.g. Printec-type technology providers) that are now in scope of NBU registration.
